<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Daniéle Prophéta
<r>Dan 8:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Anno tértio regni Baltássar regis, vísio appáruit mihi. Ego Dániel, post id quod víderam in princípio,
<n>2</n> Vidi in visióne mea, cum essem in Susis castro, quod est in Ælam regióne: vidi autem in visióne esse me super portam Ulai.
<n>3</n> Et levávi óculus meos, et vidi: et ecce áries unus stabat ante palúdem, habens córnua excélsa, et unum excélsius áltero atque succréscens.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Angústiæ mihi sunt úndique, et quid éligam ignóro;
* Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.
<r>℣.</r> Si enim hoc égero, mors mihi est; si autem non égero, non effúgiam manus vestras.
<r>℟.</r> Mélius est mihi incídere in manus hóminum, quam derelínquere legem Dei mei.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Idus Novémbris Luna duodécima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, natális beáti Martíni, Epíscopi et Confessóris; cuius vita tantis éxstitit miráculis gloriósa, ut trium mortuórum suscitátor esse merúerit.
<h>C</h>otyǽi, in Phrýgia, insígnis pássio sancti Mennæ, Ægýptii mílitis, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, postquam, abiécto milítiæ cíngulo, méruit cælésti Regi secréta conversatióne in erémo militáre, procéssit in públicum, et, se Christiánum líbera voce declárans, primo diris cruciátibus examinátur; novíssime, fixis in oratióne génibus, Dómino Iesu Christo grátias agens, gládio cæsus est, ac multis post mortem miráculis cláruit.
<h>R</h>avénnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, Feliciáni et Victoríni; qui in Diocletiáni persecutióne coronáti sunt.
<h>I</h>n Mesopotámia sancti Athenodóri Mártyris, qui, sub eódem Diocletiáno et Eléusio Prǽside, ígnibus cruciátus et áliis supplíciis tortus, demum cápitis damnátus est, et, cum cárnifex corruísset neque ullus álius gládio illum ferire ausus esset, orans obdormívit in Dómino.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Veráni Epíscopi, cuius vita fuit fide et virtútum méritis illústris.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Theodóri, Abbátis Studítæ, qui, pro fide cathólica advérsus Iconoclástas strénue pugnans, factus est apud univérsam Ecclésiam cathólicam célebris.
<h>I</h>n monastério Cryptæ Ferrátæ, in agro Tusculáno, sancti Bartholomǽi Abbátis, qui fuit sócius beáti Nili, eiúsque vitam conscrípsit.
<h>I</h>n província Sámnii beáti Mennæ solitárii, cuius virtútes et mirácula sanctus Gregórius Papa commémorat.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.6ecfb07420:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 11th 2027, the 12th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Tours, in Gaul, (in the year 397,) the blessed Confessor Martin, Bishop of that see. His life was remarkable for extraordinary miracles he raised three persons from the dead.
<h>A</h>t Cotyaeus, in Phrygia, the glorious passion of the holy Egyptian soldier Mennas. During the persecution under Diocletian he cast away his military belt, and served the King of Heaven in secret in the desert then he went forth, and freely declared himself to be a Christian. He was first examined with horrid tortures, then as he was kneeling in prayer, giving thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, he was beheaded, (in the year 305.) After his death he was famous for many miracles.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, Felician, and Victorine, who were crowned in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>I</h>n Mesopotamia, in the persecution under the same Diocletian and Eleusius the President, the holy martyr Athenodorus. He was tormented with fire and other torments, and then condemned to be beheaded but the executioner fell to the earth, and no other dared to smite him with the sword, and as he prayed he fell asleep in the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Lyon, the holy Bishop Veran, whose life was illustrious for his faith and other graces.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Constantinople, holy Theodore, of the monastery which is called the Studium who contended mightily for the Catholic faith against the Iconoclasts, and became famous throughout the whole Catholic Church, (a.d. 759-826.)
<h>I</h>n the monastery of Grotta-Ferrata, near Frascati, (in the year 1054,) the holy Abbot (of Grotta-Ferrata,) Bartholomew, a companion of blessed Nilus, and the writer of his life.
<h>I</h>n the province of Samnium, the blessed hermit, Mennas, whose graces and miracles are recorded by holy Pope Gregory.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
